text: The system shall hold each declared class of action that needs the authorization of the user.
rationale: REQ-PL-012 makes the platform tell the difference between an action that needs the authorization of the user and an action that does not, and a difference that no declaration states cannot be told. DEC-052 makes this system the one holder, because a class that each boundary keeps for itself becomes one policy for each boundary (DEC-019). MET-005 keeps the store out of the statement.

text: The system shall accept the declaration of a class, a change to a class and the removal of a class from an agent only.
rationale: REQ-PL-028 accepts a declaration from an agent only, and DEC-053 gives the reason: to structure a statement of the user into a declaration is a judgement, and DEC-030 keeps a judgement out of the platform. DEC-054 states that the reason of DEC-025 does not carry to a class, because an agent that declares a class also changes one. REQ-PL-028 states a declaration and a change to a declaration, and DEC-055 removes a class by the path that declared it, so all three name the same writer and rule 1 keeps them in one row.

text: The system shall not accept the declaration of a class, or a change to a class, until the platform records an affirmative answer to a request that states that declaration or that change.
rationale: DEC-054. The gate on the class register is stated here and is not an entry in the register, because a gate that is an entry cannot be read when the register is empty and the first class could not then be declared. DEC-049 keeps the record out of this system, so the requirement states that the platform records the answer and does not state where. A change to a class narrows it as readily as it widens it, and a narrowed class makes an action silent, so the change passes the same gate. The removal is REQ-AU-014, under REQ-PL-013.

text: The system shall give, for an action that a caller prepared and the object of that action, whether that action is in a declared class.
rationale: REQ-PL-012 needs the difference to be told before the action, and DEC-019 declares in one place and refuses in many, so this system answers and the caller refuses. The object is part of the question because a class of REQ-PL-013 cannot be judged from the action alone: to send a message to the user and to send a message to a third party are one action with two objects. DEC-057 makes the act exist before the request, so the caller states an action that it prepared and not a description of one that it intends. The answer crosses the boundary of this system, so MET-018 holds it in a row and the type is interface. OPN-025 states the norm that two rows follow, out and back.

text: The system shall accept from a caller an action that the caller prepared and the object of that action.
rationale: REQ-AU-004 cannot answer without both. MET-018 needs the contract to be held by a row that both sides name, and each boundary that asks is a supplier, so the supplying side is TBD until those systems are written. DEC-013 gives Ingestion the recognition that a change widens, which is the first supplier that the model already names. DEC-057 makes the act exist before the request.

text: The system shall give the declared classes to a caller.
rationale: REQ-PL-027 makes the rules for work with the platform agree with what the platform refuses. DEC-069 makes that agreement hold without a copy: the rules state that a declaration bounds what the platform accepts (REQ-AD-046) and carry no content (REQ-AD-047), and a caller reads the classes here at the moment that it needs them. Two statements of one register drift, which is the failure that DEC-019 states. This is an obligation at the interface and not a capability of this system, so FUN-AU-01 generates it and no third function is written. INT-PL-22 carries it to Actuation, which holds the act that gives the classes.

text: When the system cannot decide whether an action is in a declared class, the system shall give that the action is in a declared class.
rationale: RSK-AU-001 is the failure where an action that needed the user occurs with no answer, and REQ-PL-013 names actions that no person can reverse. A gate that passes what it cannot judge is not a gate. The cost is RSK-AU-002: the user is asked about actions that no class needed. The user accepts that cost while the set of declared acts is small, because an agent that reads the work that closed finds the actions that the system could not decide and proposes a class that covers them.

text: The system shall not answer a classification from a statement of the declared classes other than the statement that it gives to a caller.
rationale: RSK-AU-004. REQ-AU-006 gives the declared classes to a caller, and DEC-069 keeps that the only statement of them: REQ-AD-047 refuses a copy in the rules for work with the platform. Two statements of the same classes drift, which is the failure that DEC-019 states, and a caller cannot see the difference from outside. This row refuses the system answering from any statement but the one it gives.

text: The system shall answer a classification within TBD.
rationale: Each gated action waits for this answer before it proceeds, so this system is on the path of every gated action in the platform, as REQ-AD-015 is for a position. The value depends on the host and on which boundary asks: a boundary on a conversational path and a boundary in scheduled work do not need the same number, and neither is known. REQ-AD-015 and REQ-ST-028 carry the same TBD for the same reason. RSK-AU-006 is the failure that this answers.

text: The system shall hold, with each declared class, the writer that declared it.
rationale: REQ-ST-031 holds the writer with each declared kind for the same reason. DEC-056 makes the platform state the origin of a record, REQ-PL-029 is its product requirement, and DEC-061 makes the writer the part of the origin that the platform states. Without the writer nobody can see which agent proposed a class, and RSK-AU-005 and RSK-AU-008 are both failures that a reader finds only by reading it.

text: The system shall refuse the declaration of a class, a change to a class and the removal of a class from a caller whose position does not admit the act.
rationale: REQ-ST-032, REQ-WC-023 and REQ-AD-019 state the same refusal at the other declaration boundaries, and this system stated none, so any caller that reached it declared a class. DEC-019 makes each boundary refuse and DEC-029 makes the declaration of a class an act. REQ-PL-005 keeps an agent inside the authority that its position gives.

text: The system shall give the declared classes after the platform stops and starts.
rationale: REQ-AD-007 states the same observable for what states an agent. REQ-PL-012 cannot tell the difference between an action that needs the user and one that does not when the classes are gone, and REQ-AU-008 then answers that every action is in a declared class. A class that the user already answered for is not asked again.

text: The system shall not accept the removal of a class until the platform records an affirmative answer to a request that states that removal.
rationale: REQ-PL-013 names three classes that the user states as a hard boundary. DEC-055 makes no class permanent, so the platform does not keep the three by refusing to remove them. An earlier row in this system stated that refusal and was deleted under MET-024, because a system that obeys REQ-AU-002 and DEC-055 cannot guarantee that it holds the three. What the platform owes REQ-PL-013 is that no class is lost without an answer of the user. That the user is not told afterwards is RSK-AU-003.

text: The system shall give a copy of the declared classes that is of a state that the system held at one time.
rationale: REQ-AD-036 states the same for what states an agent. REQ-PL-022 names the declared classes, and DEC-020 gives the holder of a body the copy and the decision of when to make it, and gives External Access the carriage only. DEC-052 makes this system their one holder, so no other compartment can state what a consistent copy of them is. OPN-040 reaches this row.

text: The system shall restore the declared classes from a copy that it gave.
rationale: REQ-AD-037 states the same for what states an agent. Rule 1 keeps the copy and the restoration apart, as Agent Definition already does. REQ-PL-022 names the declared classes, and DEC-020 gives the holder of a body the copy and the decision of when to make it, and gives External Access the carriage only. DEC-052 makes this system their one holder, so no other compartment can state what a consistent copy of them is. OPN-040 reaches this row.

text: The system shall accept the declaration of a class of action that needs the authorization of the user.
rationale: REQ-PL-031. REQ-AU-001 holds each declared class, REQ-AU-002 constrains the writer and REQ-AU-003 refuses the act until the user answers. None of the three states that the system accepts the act, so the one register that REQ-PL-013 rests on had no requirement that a class can be made at all.

text: The system shall accept a change to a declared class.
rationale: REQ-PL-031. REQ-AU-003 refuses the change until the platform records an affirmative answer, which gates an act that nothing stated.

text: The system shall accept the removal of a declared class.
rationale: REQ-PL-031, DEC-055 and DEC-071. REQ-AU-014 refuses the removal until the platform records an affirmative answer, and DEC-055 states that no class is permanent, so the act was reasoned about and never stated. No declaration depends on a class.
